title: Investment Adviser (Level 2)
blurb: Advanced planning for SEBI-registered investment advisers: insurance, retirement, tax, estate, behaviour and full financial plans.

units.title: Risk management and insurance planning
units.overview: 25 marks. Identifying risks and choosing insurance to cover them.
facts: Risk management process
The process is to identify risks, measure them, choose a treatment and monitor.
An adviser lists a client's risks and assigns cover.
The process starts with buying a policy.
Risk treatment options
Risks can be avoided, reduced, retained or transferred; insurance is a way of transferring risk.
A client keeps small risks and insures large ones.
Insurance eliminates all risk.
Insurable interest
The policyholder must stand to suffer a financial loss if the insured event occurs.
A person can insure a spouse but not an unrelated stranger.
Anyone may insure anyone.
Utmost good faith
Both parties must disclose all material facts honestly, and non-disclosure can void the claim.
A client who hides a heart condition risks rejection.
Disclosure is needed only at claim time.
Indemnity
General and health insurance restore the insured to the position before the loss without allowing profit.
A fire policy pays the actual loss up to the sum insured.
Indemnity allows a claim larger than the loss.
Proximate cause
The claim is payable only if the loss arises from the insured peril as the nearest effective cause.
A loss from an excluded cause is declined.
Any loss is paid if a policy exists.
Term insurance
Term insurance pays the sum assured on death during the term and nothing on survival, so premiums are low.
A young earner buys a large term cover cheaply.
A term plan returns premiums by default.
Whole life and endowment
These combine cover with savings and are costlier per rupee of cover than term plans.
An endowment pays on maturity or death.
Endowment plans give the highest cover per premium.
ULIP
A unit linked plan invests premiums in market funds after charges, with a life cover; it has a five-year lock-in.
A policyholder switches between equity and debt funds.
ULIP returns are guaranteed.
Human life value
The human life value approach sets cover as the present value of the future earnings that the family would lose.
Cover is based on expected income over working years.
Cover equals current annual expenses only.
Needs-based approach
The needs approach adds the family's future needs and liabilities and subtracts existing assets to find the cover.
Cover covers loans, goals and living costs net of savings.
Cover is a fixed multiple for everyone.
Income multiple rule
A rough rule suggests cover of ten to fifteen times annual income, to be refined by a needs analysis.
A first estimate for a young earner.
The multiple is set by law.
Health insurance
Health policies are indemnity contracts that cover hospital costs up to the sum insured, with waiting periods for pre-existing conditions.
A person buys cover before illness arises.
Health cover applies from the first day for every condition.
Family floater and individual
A floater shares one sum insured among members, while individual policies give each person a separate sum.
A floater is cheaper but the cover can be exhausted by one member.
A floater gives each member the full sum.
Deductible and co-payment
In co-payment the insured bears a fixed share of each claim; a deductible is an amount borne before the insurer pays.
A policy requires the insured to pay 20% of each claim.
Co-payment reduces the premium to zero.
Critical illness cover
A critical illness plan pays a lump sum on diagnosis of a listed illness, regardless of the actual bills.
A benefit policy pays on diagnosis.
It reimburses only actual expenses.
Personal accident cover
Personal accident cover pays for death or disability caused by accident.
A policy pays for loss of limb in an accident.
It covers illness-related death.
Disability cover
Income protection or disability cover replaces part of earnings if the person cannot work.
A rider pays a monthly benefit on disability.
Term plans always include disability benefit.
Motor and home insurance
Third-party motor cover is mandatory; home policies cover structure and contents against listed perils.
A car owner must hold at least the liability cover.
Own-damage motor cover is compulsory.
Claim settlement ratio
The ratio of claims settled to claims received indicates an insurer's claims record, among other factors for choosing an insurer.
An adviser checks the insurer's record.
The ratio guarantees that every claim will be paid.
Nomination and assignment
A nominee receives the proceeds as a trustee in many cases, while assignment transfers rights in the policy.
A policyholder updates the nominee after marriage.
A nominee always becomes the legal owner.
Beneficiary nominee under MWP Act
A policy under the Married Women's Property Act creates a trust for the spouse and children, protecting proceeds from creditors.
A policy is protected from the policyholder's creditors.
MWP policies can be claimed by creditors.
Free-look period
A new life policy can be returned within the free-look period for a refund subject to deductions.
A buyer cancels the policy within the window.
There is no right to return a policy.
Riders
Riders add benefits such as accidental death or waiver of premium for an extra cost.
A buyer adds an accident rider.
Riders are always free.
Insurance as part of the plan
Insurance is for protection; mixing it with investment often leads to poor outcomes in both, so advisers usually separate them.
An adviser recommends term plus mutual funds.
Combination products always beat the two separately.
Emergency fund and risk
An emergency fund of three to six months of expenses is the first line of defence before insurance.
A client keeps liquid money for shocks.
An emergency fund is not needed with insurance.

units.title: Retirement planning
units.overview: 30 marks. Sizing the corpus, choosing instruments, and planning the payout.
visuals: Corpus = Annual expense at retirement / (withdrawal rate)
facts: Retirement planning
It estimates the corpus needed to sustain the client's lifestyle after income stops, and the saving needed to reach it.
A 35-year-old plans for retirement at 60.
It focuses only on the date of retirement.
Inflation impact
Inflation raises future expenses, so the corpus must be based on inflated expenses, not today's.
Expenses of ₹5 lakh today are higher at retirement.
Expenses stay constant during retirement.
Real rate of return
The real return is the return after adjusting for inflation, roughly nominal less inflation.
A return of 9% with 6% inflation is about 3% real.
The real return equals the nominal return.
Retirement corpus
The corpus is the amount that, invested at an assumed return, can fund inflation-adjusted expenses for the expected life.
The corpus covers withdrawals up to age 85 or 90.
The corpus only needs to cover five years.
Safe withdrawal rate
A safe rate such as around 4% of the initial corpus, adjusted for inflation, is used as a rule to avoid depletion.
A corpus of ₹2.5 crore supports ₹10 lakh a year.
Withdrawing 20% a year is safe.
Longevity risk
Longevity risk is the risk of outliving one's savings, addressed by planning for a long life and using annuities.
A client plans to age 90.
Longevity risk is the risk of dying early.
Sequence of returns risk
Poor returns in the early years of retirement hurt more because withdrawals deplete the corpus.
A market fall in year one damages the plan.
The order of returns does not matter.
Bucket strategy
The bucket approach holds near-term needs in safe assets and long-term money in growth assets.
Three years of expenses sit in debt funds.
All money sits in equity.
Employees' Provident Fund
The EPF is a mandatory retirement scheme where employee and employer both contribute 12% of basic pay, with a rate declared annually.
A salaried person's retirement base.
EPF offers a fixed guaranteed rate for life.
Public Provident Fund
The PPF has a 15-year tenure, an annual limit of ₹1.5 lakh and a government-set rate, with tax-free interest and maturity under current rules.
An investor opens a PPF for long-term saving.
PPF has a 5-year tenure.
National Pension System
The NPS is a market-linked pension scheme; the Tier I account has restricted withdrawals, and at 60 up to 60% may be taken as a lump sum with the rest used to buy an annuity.
A subscriber buys an annuity with part of her corpus.
NPS allows full free withdrawal at any time.
NPS asset choices
NPS subscribers choose between active choice and auto choice, with different limits for equity exposure.
An investor selects the lifecycle option.
NPS offers only government securities.
Annuity
An annuity converts a corpus into a regular income, for life or a fixed period, in exchange for a lump sum.
A retiree buys an annuity for steady income.
An annuity is a growth investment.
Immediate versus deferred annuity
An immediate annuity starts paying soon after purchase, while a deferred annuity starts after an accumulation phase.
A retiree needing income buys an immediate annuity.
A deferred annuity pays at once.
Annuity with return of purchase price
This option pays income for life and returns the purchase price to the nominee on death, with a lower payout.
A retiree wants to leave money to her heirs.
It gives a higher payout than the life-only option.
Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme
SCSS is a government scheme for those aged 60 and above with a 5-year tenure, a quarterly interest payout and an investment cap.
A retiree seeks safe regular income.
SCSS is open to all ages.
Atal Pension Yojana
APY gives a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 a month at 60 for contributors in the unorganised sector.
A small earner chooses a fixed pension.
APY pays a market-linked pension.
Systematic withdrawal plan
An SWP withdraws a fixed amount from a mutual fund regularly, providing income while the balance stays invested.
A retiree draws monthly from a debt fund.
An SWP sells the whole fund at once.
Retirement income sources
Sources include pension, rental income, interest, dividends and annuities, and the adviser should map them against expenses.
An adviser tabulates income against needs.
Only one source is needed.
Reverse mortgage
A reverse mortgage lets a senior citizen borrow against the home and receive regular payments with no repayment during life.
A homeowner draws income against the property.
The borrower makes monthly repayments.
Healthcare in retirement
Medical costs rise faster than general inflation, so health cover and a medical reserve are part of the plan.
A plan sets aside a health fund.
Healthcare costs fall after retirement.
Savings needed per month
The monthly saving is found by working out the future value of a series of investments needed to reach the corpus.
A planner solves for the SIP to reach ₹3 crore.
Savings are computed without any return assumption.
Replacement ratio
The replacement ratio is post-retirement income as a share of pre-retirement income, often taken at 60 to 80%.
A client plans for 70% of the last salary.
Replacement ratio is always 100%.
Glide path
As retirement nears, the equity share is reduced gradually to protect the corpus.
A lifecycle fund shifts to debt with age.
Equity is raised as retirement nears.
Early retirement
Retiring earlier increases the corpus needed because there are fewer saving years and more years to fund.
A client wants to retire at 45.
Early retirement lowers the required corpus.
Retirement and tax
Pension and annuity income are taxed as income, and tax on withdrawals depends on the product and the rules in force.
An annuity payout is added to taxable income.
Annuities are always tax-free.
Review and rebalancing
A retirement plan is reviewed every year for changes in expenses, returns, health and goals.
The adviser reviews assumptions annually.
A plan is set once and never reviewed.

units.title: Taxation
units.overview: 20 marks. Tax treatment of income and investments, and tax-efficient planning. Rates change; check the latest law.
visuals: Tax rates, slabs and limits change in each Budget. The facts here follow the law at the time of writing; always verify current figures before advising a client or answering a question that names a financial year.
facts: Heads of income
Income is classified as salary, house property, business or profession, capital gains and other sources.
Rent is taxed under house property.
All income is taxed under one head.
Residential status
Tax liability depends on residential status; residents are taxed on global income and non-residents on India-sourced income.
An NRI is taxed on income earned in India.
Residents are taxed only on Indian income.
Old and new regime
Individuals can choose between the old regime with deductions and the new regime with lower slab rates and few deductions.
A client with large deductions compares both.
Deductions like 80C apply under the new regime.
Section 80C
Section 80C allows a deduction up to ₹1.5 lakh for items such as PPF, ELSS, life insurance premiums and EPF in the old regime.
A client invests in ELSS for deduction.
80C allows unlimited deduction.
ELSS
Equity Linked Savings Schemes are tax-saving mutual funds with a three-year lock-in.
A client chooses ELSS under 80C.
ELSS has a 15-year lock-in.
Section 80D
Section 80D allows a deduction for health insurance premiums, with higher limits for senior citizens, in the old regime.
A client claims the premium paid for her parents.
80D covers life insurance premiums.
Section 80CCD(1B)
An additional deduction of up to ₹50,000 is available for NPS contributions, over and above 80C, in the old regime.
A client adds to NPS for extra deduction.
The extra deduction is ₹5 lakh.
Standard deduction
Salaried individuals get a flat standard deduction from salary income, and the amount differs by regime.
A salaried person gets it without any proof.
The standard deduction needs bills.
Short-term capital gains on equity
Gains on listed equity shares and equity funds held up to 12 months are short term and taxed at a flat rate, currently 20%.
A fund sold after 8 months.
Short-term gains on equity are taxed at 15% always.
Long-term capital gains on equity
Gains on listed equity held for more than 12 months are taxed at 12.5% on the amount above the annual exemption of ₹1.25 lakh.
A holder sells after two years.
LTCG on equity is fully exempt.
Debt mutual funds
Debt funds bought after April 2023 are taxed on gains at the investor's slab rate, whatever the holding period.
A debt fund gain is added to income.
Debt funds get indexation benefit.
Holding period for other assets
Unlisted shares and immovable property need two years to be long term, and long-term gains are taxed at 12.5% without indexation under current rules.
A flat sold after 3 years.
Property is long term after one year.
Gold
Gold is long term after 24 months, with gains taxed at 12.5% under current rules, while gold funds follow their own rules.
Physical gold sold after 3 years.
Gold is long term after one year.
Set-off and carry forward
Capital losses can be set off against capital gains and carried forward for eight years, but long-term losses only against long-term gains.
A short-term loss reduces long-term gain.
Long-term loss offsets any income.
Dividend taxation
Dividends are taxed in the hands of the recipient at the slab rate.
Dividend income is added to total income.
Dividends are tax-free for all investors.
Interest income
Interest from bank deposits is taxable at slab rates, with TDS above specified limits.
FD interest is added to income.
FD interest is tax-free.
TDS
Tax deducted at source is a prepayment of tax by the payer and can be adjusted in the return.
A bank deducts tax on interest.
TDS is a separate additional tax.
Advance tax
Taxpayers expecting liability above a threshold pay advance tax in instalments through the year.
A business pays four times a year.
Advance tax is paid after the year ends.
Rental income
Rent is taxed under house property after a standard deduction of 30% of net annual value, plus home loan interest deduction subject to limits.
A landlord claims a 30% deduction.
Rent is exempt from tax.
Home loan benefits
Interest on a home loan is deductible within limits for a self-occupied house, with principal repayment qualifying under 80C in the old regime.
A borrower claims interest up to the limit.
There is no tax benefit from a home loan.
HUF
A Hindu Undivided Family is taxed as a separate entity, which allows another set of exemptions and slabs.
A family splits income between itself and an HUF.
HUF is not a separate taxpayer.
Clubbing of income
Income from assets transferred to a spouse or minor child without adequate consideration is clubbed with the transferor's income.
A gift to a spouse that earns interest is taxed in the giver's hands.
Gifts to a spouse always shift the tax.
Gifts
Gifts from specified relatives are exempt, while gifts from others above a threshold are taxed as income of the recipient.
A gift from a parent is exempt.
All gifts are taxed.
Tax harvesting
Booking long-term gains up to the exemption limit each year and re-investing can reduce future tax.
An investor sells units to use the annual exemption.
Tax harvesting avoids all tax.
Tax planning versus evasion
Planning uses legal provisions to reduce tax, while evasion hides income or misreports and is illegal.
A client uses deductions properly.
Hiding income is tax planning.

units.title: Estate planning
units.overview: 20 marks. Passing wealth smoothly through wills, nominations, trusts and succession law.
facts: Estate planning
Estate planning arranges how assets will pass to the next generation, minimising disputes, delay and cost.
A client documents her wishes while alive.
It begins only after death.
Will
A will is a legal declaration of how a person wants her property distributed after death, and it takes effect only on death.
A testator names her heirs in a signed will.
A will operates from the date of signing.
Testator and executor
The testator makes the will and the executor is the person appointed to carry it out.
A friend named to execute the will.
The executor makes the will.
Valid will
A will must be in writing, signed by the testator and attested by two witnesses, and registration is optional.
A will signed before two witnesses.
Registration is compulsory.
Revoking a will
A will can be changed or revoked any time before death, and a later will overrides the earlier one.
A client writes a new will after marriage.
A will cannot be changed after signing.
Intestate succession
If a person dies without a will, the property passes according to personal succession laws.
A man dies without a will and the law decides.
The state takes the property.
Hindu Succession Act
This Act governs intestate succession among Hindus, with equal rights for sons and daughters in coparcenary property.
A daughter inherits equally.
Daughters have no rights under the Act.
Indian Succession Act
This Act governs wills and succession for Christians and others, and the rules for probate of wills.
A will's probate rules.
It applies only to Hindus.
Muslim personal law
Muslims follow personal law for succession, with defined shares, and a will is limited to a share of the estate.
A Muslim testator is limited in the portion she can will away.
A Muslim may will away the whole estate freely.
Probate
Probate is the court's certification that a will is genuine and gives the executor authority to act.
An executor obtains it to transfer assets.
Probate is a tax on the estate.
Nomination
A nominee receives assets on the holder's death but may hold them for the legal heirs, depending on the law that applies.
A bank pays a nominee and the nominee holds it for heirs.
A nominee overrides the will in all cases.
Legal heirs
Legal heirs are the persons entitled under succession law or a will, and they can claim assets irrespective of nomination in many cases.
Heirs may claim the share from the nominee.
Legal heirs have no claim if a nominee exists.
Succession certificate
A succession certificate lets the heirs of a person who died without a will collect debts and securities.
Heirs obtain it to claim bank dues.
It is required for all wills.
Trust
A trust holds property for the benefit of others under a trustee, allowing control, privacy and protection.
A settlor creates a trust for her children.
A trust is a type of will.
Settlor, trustee, beneficiary
The settlor creates the trust, the trustee manages it and the beneficiary gets the benefits.
The trustee manages assets for the beneficiary.
The beneficiary manages the trust.
Revocable and irrevocable trust
A revocable trust can be changed or ended by the settlor, while an irrevocable trust cannot, giving stronger separation of assets.
A settlor retains the power to cancel the trust.
An irrevocable trust can be withdrawn easily.
Private trust
A private trust may be set up for the family to hold assets, manage inheritance and protect minors or dependants.
A family trust holds a business stake.
A private trust must be registered as a charity.
Power of attorney
A power of attorney authorises another person to act for the principal during life and ends on the principal's death.
An agent signs documents when the owner is abroad.
A power of attorney continues after death.
Gifting
Gifting during life transfers ownership immediately via a gift deed, and property gifts require registration.
A parent gifts a flat to a child by registered deed.
An oral gift of property is valid.
Inheritance tax
India has no inheritance or estate tax at present, but income from inherited assets is taxable to the heir.
An heir pays tax on rent from an inherited flat.
India taxes the transfer on inheritance.
Cost of inherited assets
For capital gains, the cost of an inherited asset is the cost to the previous owner and the holding period includes the previous holder's period.
An heir sells an inherited house.
The cost is the value on the date of death only.
Joint holding
In a joint account with 'either or survivor', the surviving holder operates the account on the death of the other.
A spouse continues to access the account.
Joint accounts are frozen on any death.
Guardian for minors
A will can name a guardian for minor children, and a trust can manage their assets until adulthood.
A parent appoints a guardian in the will.
Minors can hold and sell property directly.
Family settlement
A family settlement is an arrangement among family members to divide property and avoid disputes.
Siblings agree on the division of assets in writing.
A family settlement needs no document.
Review of estate plan
The plan should be updated after marriage, birth, divorce, death or major changes in assets.
A client updates the will after a new child.
An estate plan never needs revision.

units.title: Behavioural finance
units.overview: 10 marks. Recognising biases in clients and in oneself.
visuals: Pain of loss > joy of gain
facts: Behavioural finance
It studies how psychology influences financial decisions and markets, in contrast to the view that investors are always rational.
A client panics and sells in a fall.
It assumes investors always act rationally.
Prospect theory
Prospect theory says people value gains and losses relative to a reference point and feel losses more strongly than equal gains.
A client dislikes a loss more than she likes the same gain.
It says people weigh gains and losses equally.
Loss aversion
Loss aversion is the tendency to feel the pain of a loss more than the pleasure of an equal gain.
A client refuses to sell a stock at a loss.
Loss aversion makes clients take more risk.
Disposition effect
Investors tend to sell winners too early and hold losers too long.
A client books a small profit but keeps a falling stock.
Investors sell losers quickly.
Anchoring
Anchoring is relying heavily on an initial number, like the purchase price, when making decisions.
A client waits for a price to return to her buying level.
Anchoring is making decisions using fresh information.
Overconfidence
Overconfident investors overestimate their knowledge and ability, trade too often and under-diversify.
A client believes she can time the market.
Overconfidence reduces trading.
Herding
Herding is following the actions of the crowd rather than one's own analysis.
Clients rush into a rising stock because others do.
Herding means making independent decisions.
Confirmation bias
Confirmation bias is seeking information that supports existing beliefs and ignoring contrary evidence.
A client reads only positive news on her holding.
It means testing views against evidence.
Recency bias
Recency bias gives too much weight to recent events and extrapolates them into the future.
A client assumes last year's rally will continue.
Recency bias values long-term history.
Availability bias
Judging the likelihood of an event by how easily examples come to mind.
A client avoids equity after hearing of a crash.
It means using full statistics.
Mental accounting
People treat money differently depending on its source or purpose, such as treating a bonus as free money.
A client spends a windfall recklessly.
It treats all money as the same.
Endowment effect
People value what they own more than identical things they do not own.
A client refuses to sell an inherited stock.
It means pricing assets at market value.
Status quo bias
A preference to keep things as they are and avoid change.
A client leaves money idle in a savings account.
It drives clients to rebalance often.
Regret aversion
Avoiding decisions that may cause regret, leading to inaction or following the crowd.
A client delays investing for fear of a fall.
It makes clients eager to take bold bets.
Framing
The way information is presented influences the decision, even when facts are the same.
A fund described as 90% success is liked more than one with 10% failure.
Framing has no effect on choices.
Cognitive and emotional biases
Cognitive biases arise from faulty reasoning and can be reduced with information, while emotional biases arise from feelings and are harder to correct, so the adviser adapts to them.
An adviser accepts an emotional bias and designs around it.
Emotional biases are easy to remove with data.
Managing client behaviour
Advisers help by setting a written policy, pre-agreeing rebalancing rules and using goal-based buckets to reduce emotional decisions.
A written plan guides a client during a fall.
Advisers should follow every client impulse.
Self-attribution
Crediting success to skill and failure to bad luck.
An investor claims her gains came from her analysis only.
Self-attribution leads to learning from errors.

units.title: Comprehensive financial advice
units.overview: 45 marks, the largest module. Putting everything together: process, regulation, risk profile, allocation, plan and review. Most case studies sit here.
focus: Goals, cash flow and net worth.
visuals: Fee cap per family per year
facts: Financial planning
Financial planning is a process of meeting life goals through the proper management of finances.
A plan links goals, cash flow, risk and investments.
It is the same as selling products.
Six-step process
The steps are establishing the relationship, gathering data, analysing, recommending, implementing and monitoring.
The adviser reviews the plan after it is implemented.
Monitoring is optional once the plan starts.
SEBI Investment Advisers Regulations
Anyone giving investment advice for a fee must be registered with SEBI under the 2013 regulations.
A fee-charging adviser needs registration.
Anyone may give paid advice without registration.
Qualification and certification
Individual advisers need prescribed qualification and a NISM certification such as Series X-A and X-B, as the rules specify.
An adviser passes the NISM certification.
No certification is required.
Fee structure
Advisers may charge a fixed fee or a fee linked to assets under advice, within a cap on fees from an individual or family per year, currently ₹1.51 lakh.
A client pays a fixed annual fee.
Advisers may take commission from products they recommend.
Segregation
Advisory and distribution activities must be separated, and advisers cannot receive distribution commission from clients they advise.
An adviser recommends direct plans.
An adviser may earn commissions from the same client.
Risk profiling
Risk profiling assesses a client's willingness, ability and need to take risk before recommending investments.
A questionnaire and cash-flow review feed the profile.
Risk profiling is based on age alone.
Risk tolerance and risk capacity
Tolerance is the willingness to bear risk, and capacity is the financial ability to bear it; the lower one governs.
A willing client with little savings gets a cautious plan.
Tolerance always determines the plan.
Suitability
Advice must be suitable to the client's profile, and the adviser must document the basis for recommendations.
A written rationale accompanies each recommendation.
Suitability is checked once a decade.
Conflict of interest
Advisers must disclose conflicts of interest and manage them in the client's favour.
An adviser discloses a relationship with a provider.
Conflicts need not be disclosed.
Risk profile report and agreement
Advisers must keep the signed agreement, risk profile and advice records for the prescribed period.
The adviser retains records for the period required.
Records are optional.
Goal-based planning
Goals are listed with amount, time horizon and priority, inflation-adjusted and matched with suitable investments.
A child's education in 12 years is funded by equity-oriented funds.
All goals are funded with the same asset.
Asset allocation
Asset allocation divides a portfolio among asset classes according to goals, horizon and risk, and drives most of the variation in returns.
A balanced client holds equity and debt.
Asset allocation is about picking one winning stock.
Strategic and tactical allocation
Strategic allocation sets long-term target weights while tactical allocation makes short-term deviations to exploit views.
A client's long-run mix is 60:40.
Tactical allocation is a fixed rule.
Rebalancing
Rebalancing returns the portfolio to target weights after market moves, by calendar or by threshold.
A portfolio is reset when equity drifts above its band.
Rebalancing means adding only to winners.
Emergency fund
The emergency fund of three to six months of expenses is kept in liquid, safe instruments.
Funds are kept in a liquid fund.
The emergency fund should be in small-cap equity.
Cash flow statement
A cash flow statement lists inflows and outflows in a period to find the surplus available for goals.
A planner finds a monthly surplus.
It shows the client's net worth.
Net worth statement
Net worth is the difference between assets and liabilities at a date.
Assets of ₹1 crore less loans of ₹30 lakh give ₹70 lakh.
Net worth is annual income minus expenses.
Debt ratios
A common guide is that EMIs should not exceed about 40% of income and total debt service should be sustainable.
A client with EMIs of 55% of income is over-leveraged.
There is no useful guide on borrowing.
Savings ratio
The savings ratio is savings as a share of income and shows the client's capacity to fund goals.
A saver putting away 25% of income.
Savings ratio is expenses divided by income.
Liquidity ratio
The liquidity ratio is liquid assets divided by monthly expenses and shows how many months the client can cope without income.
Liquid assets of ₹3 lakh with expenses of ₹50,000 give 6 months.
It measures the share of equity in the portfolio.
Time value of money
A rupee today is worth more than a rupee in the future because it can earn a return.
Planning uses present and future values.
Money has the same value at all times.
Future value
Future value is the amount an investment grows to at a given rate over a period.
₹1 lakh at 10% for 2 years becomes ₹1.21 lakh.
Future value is calculated by dividing by growth.
Present value
Present value discounts a future amount to today's equivalent at a given rate.
₹1.21 lakh in 2 years at 10% is worth ₹1 lakh today.
Present value is greater than future value for positive rates.
SIP for a goal
The monthly investment required for a goal is found from the future value of an annuity, given the expected return and time.
A planner sets the SIP for a target corpus.
A SIP amount does not depend on time horizon.
CAGR
The compound annual growth rate expresses the annualised growth between two values over a period.
₹100 growing to ₹200 in 5 years is about 14.9% a year.
CAGR is the simple average of yearly returns.
Time-weighted return
Time-weighted return removes the effect of cash flows to measure the manager's performance.
A fund's return is compared over a period fairly.
It depends on the timing of the client's deposits.
Sharpe ratio
The Sharpe ratio is excess return over the risk-free rate divided by standard deviation and measures return per unit of total risk.

mocks.w: Gifts: Gifts from specified relatives are exempt, while gifts from others above a threshold are taxed as income of the recipient.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Retirement corpus”?
o: Risks can be avoided, reduced, retained or transferred; insurance is a way of transferring risk.
The corpus is the amount that, invested at an assumed return, can fund inflation-adjusted expenses for the expected life.
In case questions, extract the client's goals, income, assets, liabilities, risk profile and assumptions into a table before answering.
India has no inheritance or estate tax at present, but income from inherited assets is taxable to the heir.
mocks.w: Retirement corpus: The corpus is the amount that, invested at an assumed return, can fund inflation-adjusted expenses for the expected life.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Reverse mortgage” is correct?
o: The borrower makes monthly repayments.
Anchoring is making decisions using fresh information.
A reverse mortgage lets a senior citizen borrow against the home and receive regular payments with no repayment during life.
Advisers are not subject to complaints.
mocks.w: Correct: A reverse mortgage lets a senior citizen borrow against the home and receive regular payments with no repayment during life.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Insurable interest” is correct?
o: Gold is long term after one year.
The policyholder must stand to suffer a financial loss if the insured event occurs.
Anyone may insure anyone.
One standard plan fits every client.
mocks.w: Correct: The policyholder must stand to suffer a financial loss if the insured event occurs.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Claim settlement ratio”?
o: Interest on a home loan is deductible within limits for a self-occupied house, with principal repayment qualifying under 80C in the old regime.
An immediate annuity starts paying soon after purchase, while a deferred annuity starts after an accumulation phase.
The ratio of claims settled to claims received indicates an insurer's claims record, among other factors for choosing an insurer.
Cognitive biases arise from faulty reasoning and can be reduced with information, while emotional biases arise from feelings and are harder to correct, so the adviser adapts to them.
mocks.w: Claim settlement ratio: The ratio of claims settled to claims received indicates an insurer's claims record, among other factors for choosing an insurer.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Health insurance”?
o: Health policies are indemnity contracts that cover hospital costs up to the sum insured, with waiting periods for pre-existing conditions.
Overconfident investors overestimate their knowledge and ability, trade too often and under-diversify.
Retiring earlier increases the corpus needed because there are fewer saving years and more years to fund.
Strategic allocation sets long-term target weights while tactical allocation makes short-term deviations to exploit views.
mocks.w: Health insurance: Health policies are indemnity contracts that cover hospital costs up to the sum insured, with waiting periods for pre-existing conditions.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Clients can complain to the adviser, then SEBI through its portal, and the adviser must act on complaints promptly.
o: Grievance redressal
Family floater and individual
Emergency fund
Savings ratio
mocks.w: Grievance redressal: Clients can complain to the adviser, then SEBI through its portal, and the adviser must act on complaints promptly.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Present value” is correct?
o: Present value is greater than future value for positive rates.
There is no tax benefit from a home loan.
Present value discounts a future amount to today's equivalent at a given rate.
Risk profiling is based on age alone.
mocks.w: Correct: Present value discounts a future amount to today's equivalent at a given rate.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Risk profiling” is correct?
o: Risk profiling assesses a client's willingness, ability and need to take risk before recommending investments.
An oral gift of property is valid.
Risk profiling is based on age alone.
Investors sell losers quickly.
mocks.w: Correct: Risk profiling assesses a client's willingness, ability and need to take risk before recommending investments.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The steps are establishing the relationship, gathering data, analysing, recommending, implementing and monitoring.
o: Herding
Strategic and tactical allocation
Six-step process
Client communication
mocks.w: Six-step process: The steps are establishing the relationship, gathering data, analysing, recommending, implementing and monitoring.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Emergency fund” is correct?
o: A family settlement needs no document.
An irrevocable trust can be withdrawn easily.
The emergency fund of three to six months of expenses is kept in liquid, safe instruments.
The emergency fund should be in small-cap equity.
mocks.w: Correct: The emergency fund of three to six months of expenses is kept in liquid, safe instruments.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Cost of inherited assets” is correct?
o: The cost is the value on the date of death only.
It focuses only on the date of retirement.
MWP policies can be claimed by creditors.
For capital gains, the cost of an inherited asset is the cost to the previous owner and the holding period includes the previous holder's period.
mocks.w: Correct: For capital gains, the cost of an inherited asset is the cost to the previous owner and the holding period includes the previous holder's period.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Atal Pension Yojana” is correct?
o: Anchoring is making decisions using fresh information.
APY gives a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 a month at 60 for contributors in the unorganised sector.
APY pays a market-linked pension.
An SWP sells the whole fund at once.
mocks.w: Correct: APY gives a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 a month at 60 for contributors in the unorganised sector.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? NPS subscribers choose between active choice and auto choice, with different limits for equity exposure.
o: Proximate cause
Motor and home insurance
Cognitive and emotional biases
NPS asset choices
mocks.w: NPS asset choices: NPS subscribers choose between active choice and auto choice, with different limits for equity exposure.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Interest on a home loan is deductible within limits for a self-occupied house, with principal repayment qualifying under 80C in the old regime.
o: Home loan benefits
NPS asset choices
Debt ratios
Succession certificate
mocks.w: Home loan benefits: Interest on a home loan is deductible within limits for a self-occupied house, with principal repayment qualifying under 80C in the old regime.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? These combine cover with savings and are costlier per rupee of cover than term plans.
o: Trust
Whole life and endowment
Savings needed per month
ULIP
mocks.w: Whole life and endowment: These combine cover with savings and are costlier per rupee of cover than term plans.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Set-off and carry forward” is correct?
o: Money has the same value at all times.
A will operates from the date of signing.
Capital losses can be set off against capital gains and carried forward for eight years, but long-term losses only against long-term gains.
Long-term loss offsets any income.
mocks.w: Correct: Capital losses can be set off against capital gains and carried forward for eight years, but long-term losses only against long-term gains.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Short-term capital gains on equity” is correct?
o: It measures the share of equity in the portfolio.
Short-term gains on equity are taxed at 15% always.
Gains on listed equity shares and equity funds held up to 12 months are short term and taxed at a flat rate, currently 20%.
The executor makes the will.
mocks.w: Correct: Gains on listed equity shares and equity funds held up to 12 months are short term and taxed at a flat rate, currently 20%.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Gold is long term after 24 months, with gains taxed at 12.5% under current rules, while gold funds follow their own rules.
o: Sequence of returns risk
Gold
Annuity
Probate
mocks.w: Gold: Gold is long term after 24 months, with gains taxed at 12.5% under current rules, while gold funds follow their own rules.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Riders” is correct?
o: Riders are always free.
Riders add benefits such as accidental death or waiver of premium for an extra cost.
Conflicts need not be disclosed.
It covers illness-related death.
mocks.w: Correct: Riders add benefits such as accidental death or waiver of premium for an extra cost.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Hindu Succession Act” is correct?
o: A term plan returns premiums by default.
Daughters have no rights under the Act.
Self-attribution leads to learning from errors.
This Act governs intestate succession among Hindus, with equal rights for sons and daughters in coparcenary property.
mocks.w: Correct: This Act governs intestate succession among Hindus, with equal rights for sons and daughters in coparcenary property.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Settlor, trustee, beneficiary” is correct?
o: Tactical allocation is a fixed rule.
Overconfidence reduces trading.
The beneficiary manages the trust.
The settlor creates the trust, the trustee manages it and the beneficiary gets the benefits.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Prospect theory says people value gains and losses relative to a reference point and feel losses more strongly than equal gains.

Prospect theory
Debt ratios
Probate

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Strategic and tactical allocation”?
o: A will can be changed or revoked any time before death, and a later will overrides the earlier one.
Asset allocation divides a portfolio among asset classes according to goals, horizon and risk, and drives most of the variation in returns.
Strategic allocation sets long-term target weights while tactical allocation makes short-term deviations to exploit views.
Equity Linked Savings Schemes are tax-saving mutual funds with a three-year lock-in.
mocks.w: Strategic and tactical allocation: Strategic allocation sets long-term target weights while tactical allocation makes short-term deviations to exploit views.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Regret aversion” is correct?
o: MWP policies can be claimed by creditors.
Avoiding decisions that may cause regret, leading to inaction or following the crowd.
CAPM uses standard deviation as the risk.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Individuals can choose between the old regime with deductions and the new regime with lower slab rates and few deductions.

Old and new regime
Diversification
Inheritance tax

mocks.p: Which statement about “Debt ratios” is correct?

A trust is a type of will.

mocks.w: Correct: A common guide is that EMIs should not exceed about 40% of income and total debt service should be sustainable.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? As retirement nears, the equity share is reduced gradually to protect the corpus.

Net worth statement

Future value is the amount an investment grows to at a given rate over a period.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Proximate cause” is correct?

Suitability

An immediate annuity starts paying soon after purchase, while a deferred annuity starts after an accumulation phase.
Overconfidence reduces trading.
Conflicts need not be disclosed.

Systematic withdrawal plan
Residential status

Proximate cause

The human life value approach sets cover as the present value of the future earnings that the family would lose.

Endowment plans give the highest cover per premium.

Tax deducted at source is a prepayment of tax by the payer and can be adjusted in the return.
Muslims follow personal law for succession, with defined shares, and a will is limited to a share of the estate.

Review and rebalancing
Grievance redressal

The emergency fund should be in small-cap equity.

mocks.p: Which statement about “NPS asset choices” is correct?

NPS subscribers choose between active choice and auto choice, with different limits for equity exposure.

NPS offers only government securities.

Diversification
Anchoring
Gold

Power of attorney
Dividend taxation
Term insurance

Tolerance is the willingness to bear risk, and capacity is the financial ability to bear it; the lower one governs.
Tolerance always determines the plan.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Private trust”?

Probate is the court's certification that a will is genuine and gives the executor authority to act.
A private trust may be set up for the family to hold assets, manage inheritance and protect minors or dependants.

Records are optional.
CAPM uses standard deviation as the risk.

Overconfidence reduces trading.
Self-attribution leads to learning from errors.

Holding period for other assets
NPS asset choices
Qualification and certification

Financial planning
Nomination

A safe rate such as around 4% of the initial corpus, adjusted for inflation, is used as a rule to avoid depletion.

Interest income
Behavioural finance

Diversification

o: Indemnity
Mutual fund selection
Replacement ratio
Strategic and tactical allocation

Review of estate plan
Conflict of interest
Revocable and irrevocable trust

mocks.p: Which statement about “Insurance as part of the plan” is correct?

One standard plan fits every client.

An SWP sells the whole fund at once.

The adviser's duty is to maximise her fee.
It depends on the timing of the client's deposits.
A term plan returns premiums by default.

Client communication
Fee structure
Real rate of return

o: Conflicts need not be disclosed.

Direct plans carry higher costs.

o: Asset allocation is about picking one winning stock.
Minors can hold and sell property directly.
Term insurance pays the sum assured on death during the term and nothing on survival, so premiums are low.
A term plan returns premiums by default.

o: A Muslim may will away the whole estate freely.
The Sharpe ratio uses beta as the risk measure.
Only one source is needed.
The Sharpe ratio is excess return over the risk-free rate divided by standard deviation and measures return per unit of total risk.

Insurable interest
Health insurance
Inflation impact

Managing client behaviour
Qualification and certification
Revocable and irrevocable trust

mocks.p: Which statement about “Recency bias” is correct?

It assumes investors always act rationally.
Herding means making independent decisions.
Recency bias gives too much weight to recent events and extrapolates them into the future.

The monthly saving is found by working out the future value of a series of investments needed to reach the corpus.
Suitability is checked once a decade.
Any loss is paid if a policy exists.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Medical costs rise faster than general inflation, so health cover and a medical reserve are part of the plan.
o: Sharpe ratio
Conflict of interest
Tax planning versus evasion
Healthcare in retirement

mocks.p: Which statement about “Retirement and tax” is correct?
o: Annuities are always tax-free.
No certification is required.
It depends on the timing of the client's deposits.
Pension and annuity income are taxed as income, and tax on withdrawals depends on the product and the rules in force.
mocks.w: Correct: Pension and annuity income are taxed as income, and tax on withdrawals depends on the product and the rules in force.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Time value of money” is correct?
o: There is no tax benefit from a home loan.
A rupee today is worth more than a rupee in the future because it can earn a return.
It reimburses only actual expenses.
Money has the same value at all times.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Net worth statement”?
o: Salaried individuals get a flat standard deduction from salary income, and the amount differs by regime.
The liquidity ratio is liquid assets divided by monthly expenses and shows how many months the client can cope without income.
The real return is the return after adjusting for inflation, roughly nominal less inflation.
Net worth is the difference between assets and liabilities at a date.
mocks.w: Net worth statement: Net worth is the difference between assets and liabilities at a date.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme” is correct?

Diversification removes market risk entirely.
SCSS is open to all ages.
The state takes the property.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Liquidity ratio” is correct?
o: The liquidity ratio is liquid assets divided by monthly expenses and shows how many months the client can cope without income.
It measures the share of equity in the portfolio.
Money has the same value at all times.
An estate plan never needs revision.
mocks.w: Correct: The liquidity ratio is liquid assets divided by monthly expenses and shows how many months the client can cope without income.

mocks.p: Which statement best describes “Client communication”?
o: Taxpayers expecting liability above a threshold pay advance tax in instalments through the year.
NPS subscribers choose between active choice and auto choice, with different limits for equity exposure.
Communication should be clear, in the client's language, honest about risks and avoiding jargon and promises.
The testator makes the will and the executor is the person appointed to carry it out.
mocks.w: Client communication: Communication should be clear, in the client's language, honest about risks and avoiding jargon and promises.

mocks.p: Which statement about “CAGR” is correct?
o: The compound annual growth rate expresses the annualised growth between two values over a period.
Health cover applies from the first day for every condition.
CAGR is the simple average of yearly returns.
The corpus only needs to cover five years.

o: Monitoring is optional once the plan starts.
The adviser's duty is to maximise her fee.
The adviser acts in the client's best interest, with integrity, confidentiality and care.
APY pays a market-linked pension.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? A preference to keep things as they are and avoid change.
o: Nomination and assignment
Status quo bias
ULIP
Heads of income
mocks.w: Status quo bias: A preference to keep things as they are and avoid change.

mocks.p: Which statement about “SEBI Investment Advisers Regulations” is correct?
o: Replacement ratio is always 100%.

Anyone giving investment advice for a fee must be registered with SEBI under the 2013 regulations.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Will” is correct?
o: Legal heirs have no claim if a nominee exists.
A will operates from the date of signing.
A will is a legal declaration of how a person wants her property distributed after death, and it takes effect only on death.
LTCG on equity is fully exempt.

Testator and executor
Availability bias
Inheritance tax

mocks.p: Which statement about “Annuity with return of purchase price” is correct?

Short-term gains on equity are taxed at 15% always.

One standard plan fits every client.
A term plan returns premiums by default.
Reviews are only needed on request.

A retirement plan is reviewed every year for changes in expenses, returns, health and goals.
Present value discounts a future amount to today's equivalent at a given rate.

There is no right to return a policy.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Status quo bias” is correct?
o: It drives clients to rebalance often.
A preference to keep things as they are and avoid change.
It makes clients eager to take bold bets.
Emotional biases are easy to remove with data.
mocks.w: Correct: A preference to keep things as they are and avoid change.

A nominee overrides the will in all cases.

Proximate cause
Human life value
Whole life and endowment

Riders

Ethics and fiduciary duty

Present value

Indian Succession Act
Private trust

Savings needed per month

Atal Pension Yojana
Retirement corpus
Safe withdrawal rate

80D covers life insurance premiums.
Salaried individuals get a flat standard deduction from salary income, and the amount differs by regime.
LTCG on equity is fully exempt.

mocks.p: A willing client with little savings gets a cautious plan. Which idea does this illustrate?

Net worth statement
Asset allocation
Risk tolerance and risk capacity

Financial planning
Client communication

Confirmation bias
Status quo bias

Segregation
Client communication

Diversification
Emergency fund

Regret aversion
Overconfidence
Confirmation bias

Early retirement lowers the required corpus.
A deferred annuity pays at once.
An annuity is a growth investment.

Healthcare costs fall after retirement.
Medical costs rise faster than general inflation, so health cover and a medical reserve are part of the plan.

Goal-based planning
Special situations
